Reading R files from elsewhere

Source: vignettes/safe-reading.Rmd
safe-reading.Rmd
library(zurds)
ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "zurds")

An .rds or .rda file is a serialized R object, and R objects can hold code. readRDS() and load() rebuild everything in the file: closures, environments, promises. Since R 4.4.0 a promise at the top level of a file is refused (CVE-2024-27322), but a promise nested in a list, a closure or an environment still loads, and runs when used.

zurds reads the file without R’s deserializer. This vignette shows how to look before you load, and what its data-only reader does and does not promise.

Look first

rds_info() reads only the header. rds_str() and rds_toc() walk the whole stream but build nothing: a 2 GB .rda costs the time to decompress it, not the memory to hold it.

rds_info(ex("model.rds"))
#> <rds_info>
#> kind:               rds
#> format:             xdr, version 3
#> written by R:       4.6.1
#> readable from R:    3.5.0
#> native encoding:    UTF-8
#> compression:        gzip
rds_str(ex("model.rds"))
#> List of 2
#>  $ data:'data.frame':    6 obs. of  2 variables:
#>   ..$ mpg: num [1:6]
#>   ..$ wt: num [1:6]
#>  $ fit:'lm' List of 12
#>   ..$ coefficients: num [1:2]
#>   ..$ residuals: num [1:32]
#>   ..$ effects: num [1:32]
#>   ..$ rank: int [1:1]
#>   ..$ fitted.values: num [1:32]
#>   ..$ assign: int [1:2]
#>   ..$ qr:'qr' List of 5
#>   ..$ df.residual: int [1:1]
#>   ..$ xlevels:List of 0
#>   ..$ call: language
#>   ..$ terms: 'terms', 'formula' language
#>   ..$ model:'data.frame':    32 obs. of  2 variables:
rds_toc(ex("objects.rda"))
#>        name    type      class length     dim size offset risky
#> 1      cars    list data.frame     11 10 x 11 1396     48 FALSE
#> 2   species integer     factor      3    <NA>  133   1467 FALSE
#> 3      grid  double       <NA>      6   2 x 3   95   1620 FALSE
#> 4 summarise closure       <NA>      1    <NA>  132   1740  TRUE

Scan

rds_scan() lists everything that can run code ("executes"), reach outside the file ("reaches_out"), or needs a package to load ("needs_package"), with where it is:

rds_scan(ex("model.rds"))
#>                                                                  path
#> 1                                            [[2]][[11]]$.Environment
#> 2       [[2]][[11]]$.Environment@hashtab[[11]]$fit[[11]]$.Environment
#> 3 [[2]][[11]]$.Environment@hashtab[[11]]$fit[[12]]$terms$.Environment
#> 4                                      [[2]][[12]]$terms$.Environment
#>       finding detail    severity
#> 1 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 2 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 3 environment   <NA> reaches_out
#> 4 environment   <NA> reaches_out
rds_scan(ex("promise.rds"))
#>    path finding detail severity
#> 1 [[2]] promise   <NA> executes
rds_deps(serialize(stats::sd, NULL))
#>   package    reason detail
#> 1   stats namespace   <NA>

A linear model carries its formula’s environment: loading it gives you that environment back. The second file holds a promise whose code would call system().

Read data, refuse code

rds_read_data() is a reader written in C that builds only NULL, logical, integer, double, complex, character, raw and list vectors, with their attributes. For a data-only file its result is identical() to readRDS().

identical(rds_read_data(ex("iris.rds")), readRDS(ex("iris.rds")))
#> [1] TRUE

Anything else is an error, with the scan attached:

cnd <- tryCatch(rds_read_data(ex("promise.rds")),
                zurds_unsafe_content = function(e) e)
cnd$findings
#>    path finding detail severity
#> 1 [[2]] promise   <NA> executes

or, with strict = FALSE, replaced by NULL with a warning:

rds_read_data(ex("promise.rds"), strict = FALSE)
#> Warning in rds_read_data(ex("promise.rds"), strict = FALSE): replaced 1 promise
#> item(s) by NULL
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "harmless"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> NULL

rds_extract() reads one object, list element or column the same way, and rds_lazyload_extract() one object of a lazy-load database.

What the guarantee covers

rds_read_data():

  1. never calls unserialize(), eval() or any function from the file;
  2. builds only the types above, with attributes of those types; a class attribute is kept, and no method of that class is called while building;
  3. refuses, or with strict = FALSE drops, every other type;
  4. checks every length and depth against its limits before allocating.

What it does not cover: once you have the object, your own code may dispatch on its class to methods you have loaded. A data frame is still a data frame, and a class name from the file can still select a print() method in your session. That is your code, not the file’s.

rds_scan() and rds_is_safe() are advisory for readRDS(): a clean scan means the file holds no type that runs code as it loads, but readRDS() still creates objects of the file’s classes. When you trust a file’s code, rds_extract(use_r = TRUE) hands one item, and only that item, to R’s own reader, with its scan attached.
